wait "$writer"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Quitting top preserves the shell INT, TERM, HUP and WINCH traps.

files.snap/meminfo:
MemTotal: 1024 kB
MemAvailable: 256 kB
SwapTotal: 512 kB
SwapFree: 128 kB
files.traps.sh:
/usr/bin/mount -n --bind "$PWD/snap" /proc || exit 91
trap 'printf term-trap\n' TERM
trap 'printf hup-trap\n' HUP
trap 'printf winch-trap\n' WINCH
trap 'printf int-trap\n' INT
trap -p TERM HUP WINCH INT > "$HOME/traps-before.txt"
before=$(< "$HOME/traps-before.txt")
top -d 2
rc=$?
printf "%s\n" "$rc" > "$HOME/traps-top-status.txt"
trap -p TERM HUP WINCH INT > "$HOME/traps-after.txt"
after=$(< "$HOME/traps-after.txt")
if [[ $before == "$after" && $rc == 0 ]]; then printf 'TRAPS-RESTORED\n'; else printf 'TRAPS-CHANGED\n'; exit 1; fi

cases.oracle: BashOS top documented interactive controls over an independently encoded private proc(5) snapshot; xterm/ECMA-48 controls and PTY modes are decoded independently by the harness.
cases.comparison: Private snapshot overlay validated in a fresh user namespace; raw PTY bytes, steps, decoded screen, status and initial/final terminal modes retained. Only reached actions are evidence. The exact shell trap definitions before and after top, and its numeric exit status, are retained as diagnostics.
